ideas.title: How a Cold Case Investigation Actually Works, From First Report to Final Arrest
ideas.hook: Most cold cases are not solved by a genius. They are solved by a box of evidence somebody packaged properly thirty years ago.
ideas.angle: A process explainer using a clearly labelled composite case, every step sourced to NIJ, DOJ and FBI publications.
ideas.rationale: Evergreen, high search interest, needs no case-specific footage; documents and public-domain material carry it.

ideas.title: What a CODIS Hit Really Means (And What It Doesn't)
ideas.hook: A database match is the moment most documentaries treat as the ending. In court, it is barely the beginning.
ideas.angle: Walks through local, state and national DNA index levels and match confirmation, using FBI publications.
ideas.rationale: Strong explainer demand, few calm treatments; federal documents are public domain.

ideas.title: Genetic Genealogy: How a Family Tree Becomes a Lead
ideas.hook: You never took a DNA test. Your third cousin did.
ideas.angle: Explains forensic genetic genealogy and the 2019 DOJ interim policy, with the privacy debate presented fairly.
ideas.rationale: High interest; crowded but often sensational, so a sourced, balanced take can stand out.

ideas.title: Reading a Probable Cause Affidavit, Line by Line
ideas.hook: The most detailed account of an arrest is usually public, and almost nobody reads it.
ideas.angle: Teaches viewers to read a real affidavit from a resolved case chosen from court records at research time.
ideas.rationale: Low competition; the document itself is the footage.

ideas.title: Cleared but Never Tried: When a Case Closes Without a Courtroom
ideas.hook: A family can be told their case is solved and never see anyone stand trial.
ideas.angle: Explains clearance by exceptional means using FBI UCR definitions and a resolved case from the record.
ideas.rationale: Distinctive angle centred on families; definitions are public.

ideas.title: The Evidence Room: Where Cold Cases Wait
ideas.hook: Every unsolved case has an address. It is a shelf.
ideas.angle: Evidence retention, chain of custody and what happens when evidence is lost, from agency policy documents.
ideas.rationale: Under-covered topic; agency-released facility tours are sometimes available.

ideas.title: Why Some Agencies Have Cold Case Units and Others Don't
ideas.hook: Whether your case gets a second look can depend on a grant that ran out.
ideas.angle: Funding and sustainability of cold case units, sourced to the NIJ 2019 best-practices guide.
ideas.rationale: Policy angle few channels cover; supports later single-case episodes.

ideas.title: Bodycam Footage: Who Decides What the Public Sees
ideas.hook: Two identical recordings can be public in one state and sealed in the next.
ideas.angle: Compares release rules across a few states using official policy documents, no incident footage needed.
ideas.rationale: Strong interest; explains the rules this channel itself follows.

ideas.title: A Resolved 1980s Homicide Solved by Retesting Old Evidence
ideas.hook: The answer had been in the evidence room the whole time.
ideas.angle: Single-case deep dive on a case selected at research time from court records where a conviction is final.
ideas.rationale: Template slot: case chosen only if court records and an official release exist.

ideas.title: The Witness Who Came Back: Re-Interviewing After Decades
ideas.hook: Some witnesses do not lie the first time. They just are not ready to tell the truth.
ideas.angle: How investigators re-approach witnesses without contaminating memory, drawn from published interview guidance.
ideas.rationale: Human angle; relies on documents and court testimony transcripts.

ideas.title: Unidentified Remains: How a Name Is Returned
ideas.hook: Before a case can be solved, sometimes the victim has to be identified.
ideas.angle: How NamUs, DNA and genealogy are used to identify remains; one resolved identification from official releases.
ideas.rationale: Respectful, victim-centred topic with official releases available.

ideas.title: What Happens After the Arrest: A Cold Case in Court
ideas.hook: The arrest makes the news. The two years after it rarely do.
ideas.angle: Follows a resolved cold case through docket entries from charge to verdict.
ideas.rationale: Court video and dockets are often public for resolved cases.

ideas.title: When the Original Investigation Got It Wrong
ideas.hook: Reopening a case can mean admitting the first answer was not the right one.
ideas.angle: A case where a conviction was vacated and the record was corrected, sourced to court rulings.
ideas.rationale: Important, high interest; must be chosen from cases with final court rulings.

ideas.title: The Families Who Wait: Living With an Unsolved Case
ideas.hook: For the people left behind, a cold case is not cold.
ideas.angle: Victim-centred episode using public statements families chose to make, with consent-based framing.
ideas.rationale: Pillar-defining episode; uses only public, family-authorised statements.

ideas.title: Chain of Custody: The Paperwork That Wins or Loses a Case
ideas.hook: A single missing signature can matter more than the DNA.
ideas.angle: Explains chain of custody with real evidence forms (blank templates) and court rulings on breaks in custody.
ideas.rationale: Low competition, document-driven.

ideas.title: Familial Searching vs Genetic Genealogy: Not the Same Thing
ideas.hook: Two DNA techniques, two sets of rules, constantly confused.
ideas.angle: Side-by-side explainer using DOJ policy and state laws.
ideas.rationale: Clarifies a common confusion; strong for search.

ideas.title: The 911 Call: What the First Minutes Record
ideas.hook: The first recording in a case is often a voice, not a video.
ideas.angle: How emergency call records are kept and released, with privacy redactions; no graphic audio used.
ideas.rationale: Interest is high; release terms vary, so footage feasibility is moderate.

ideas.title: Statutes of Limitation and Murder: Why Some Cases Can Never Close
ideas.hook: For most crimes the clock runs out. For murder, in most states, it never starts.
ideas.angle: Legal explainer with a disclaimer; sourced to statutes and court opinions.
ideas.rationale: Evergreen legal topic; needs a legal disclaimer line.

ideas.title: A Cold Case Solved by a Single Fingerprint
ideas.hook: Fingerprints were collected in the original investigation. The database to search them came later.
ideas.angle: Single-case deep dive chosen from resolved cases with public court records; explains AFIS/NGI history.
ideas.rationale: Template slot requiring a case with final court records.

ideas.title: How Investigators Choose Which Cold Cases to Reopen
ideas.hook: There are more unsolved cases than investigators. Someone has to choose.
ideas.angle: Case selection criteria from the NIJ guide, told through a composite review.
ideas.rationale: Under-covered; pairs with the flagship explainer.

ideas.title: The Press Conference: Reading Between the Lines
ideas.hook: What police say at a podium is chosen carefully. So is what they leave out.
ideas.angle: Uses officially released press conferences from resolved cases to show how information is managed.
ideas.rationale: Press conferences are commonly released and usable with attribution.

ideas.title: Evidence That Was Destroyed: When a Cold Case Can't Be Reopened
ideas.hook: Sometimes the reason a case stays unsolved is a retention schedule.
ideas.angle: Evidence retention laws and their consequences, sourced to statutes and audits.
ideas.rationale: Distinctive; relies on documents.

ideas.title: Two Investigations, One Case: Then and Now
ideas.hook: Same file, same evidence, thirty years apart.
ideas.angle: Side-by-side of 1990s and current methods using a resolved case from court records.
ideas.rationale: Strong format for the channel; depends on available court records.

ideas.title: What 'Person of Interest' Actually Means
ideas.hook: It is not a legal term, and it can follow someone for life.
ideas.angle: Explains investigative language and the harm of public speculation; legal disclaimer included.
ideas.rationale: Reinforces the channel's no-speculation rule; easy to source.
